Austin (taken to be the legal theorist John Austin) is called a "naive empiricist" because his account of law rests on an anachronistic model of a legal system. That model reduces law to observable facts, such as a sovereign's habitually obeyed commands backed by sanctions. It leaves out the rules, officials and institutions that actually make up a legal system. I'm relying on the team note for this and can't independently confirm that the phrase appears in a specific source.

CONFIDENCE: 40
